newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bonds suffered along with the German market on Tuesday, closing lower as concern about European monetary union drove up the dollar.
French traders were also catching up after the long holiday weekend and the market remained relatively calm as strong liquidity stemmed fears of a bigger sell-off.

The market is awaiting the results of an audit of French public finances due on July 21, though much of the bad news has already been trailed in advance. The audit is expected to show the public deficit running at 3.5 to 3.7 percent of gross domestic product this year without corrective measures.
One analyst said the market had already discounted the bad news in the French audit. "There would really have to be a very bad shock for things to fall apart," he said.
Dealers said they expected fairly calm trading on Wednesday and said there could be some recovery in prices.

Technically, the September 10-year bond future, which broke through support on Tuesday at 130.04/06 to close at 129.98, should trade between 129.70/80 and 130.16/18. It might even test its contract high of 130.88, one operator said.

Markets are also awaiting Thursday's BTAN auction, the first time France is selling notes in francs and ecus with the same characteristics to make them easily interchangeable after the launch of the euro.
The Treasury said on Tuesday it would sell 19 to 21 billion francs and 600 to 800 million ecus of 4.50 percent BTANS, due July 12, 2002, on Thursday.
